Verified differentially. Old commits: R0 on 26642c72 (a fabricated 5-field meta with no transcript passes), N1a on 83860be3 (a pre-freeze LOAD run with another assignment closes a finding), and round-3 test 7 on 540b3c69 (a verifying record without 'assignment' skips the assignment binding) all reproduce (02/03/04 logs). Accepted, disclosed residual (D-021): run evidence is self-hashed, not attested. The narrower gap in what the outputs binding proves is raised separately as F-DG0-119 (Low).

On 26642c72, R4 reproduces: '#', '.' and non-path evidence are accepted (02 log). On candidate 53f5d176, repro-r4 test 18 rejects '#', '.', a directory, a bare token and a '<file>/..' path as gate test evidence, and rejects an empty tests[]. Test 15 shows verification evidence '#' is rejected too.

On 26642c72, R5 reproduces: text after a closing quote is accepted (02 log). On candidate 53f5d176, repro-r4 test 19: text after a quote, long rows, short rows, a stray quote and an unterminated quote all throw. I also inspected tools/gates/lib/csv.mjs directly: header and register checks require exact column lists, so duplicate header names cannot pass silently.

I ran the real runner (candidate run-agent.sh) in a disposable clone with a stub claude (06-runner-e2e.log). --role 'x;id' and --task 'T$(id)' are rejected (exit 64). An assignment outside the repository is rejected (exit 66). Run IDs carry the session-ID prefix, and 'mkdir "$OUT"' (without -p) refuses an existing directory. The agent's exit status propagates to meta.exit_code and to the runner's exit status (FAKE_EXIT=3 gives 3). The prompt is passed as one argv element, so assignment content never reaches a shell. Round-2 evidence of the original weakness is in round-2/06-runner-and-hook.log. New runner issues are raised separately (F-DG0-119, F-DG0-120).

It declares 'permissions: contents: read', uses fetch-depth 0, has no secrets, and runs validate.mjs --pipeline without continue-on-error, so a failure fails the job (10-docs-ci.log).

On 83860be3, N1b (the reporter's sidecar says FAIL while findings.json says CLOSED_VERIFIED) and N1c (unchecked evidence and fix_revision) pass the gate (03 log). On candidate 53f5d176, repro-r4 test 15: a reporter's FAIL sidecar entry, a fix_revision outside the verified round's candidate, and non-file verification evidence are each rejected. Test 2 confirms a genuine FAIL keeps the gate closed. Closure is read from bound reviewer sidecars. Forging a committed sidecar inside a merge commit is tracked under F-DG0-115.

On 83860be3, N4 (a file containing 'symlink:<t>' collides with a symlink) and N5 (the exec bit is not hashed) reproduce (03 log). 10-docs-ci.log at 53f5d176: D-019, agents.md and agent-protocol.md all say resumes happen 'up to 6 times', matching MTH_MAX_RESUMES default 6 in run-agent.sh:22. agents.md lists the protected set as write-scopes.json has it. D-016/D-018 are consistent with the verification binding. The new D-021 overstatement about 'exact bytes' is raised separately as F-DG0-119, not as a regression of this finding.

Partly fixed, but the write-once rule can be bypassed with a merge commit. Fixed: on 540b3c69, round-3 tests 4-6 reproduce the original edits (04 log). On candidate 53f5d176, the same edits made in an ordinary commit or in the working tree are rejected ('write-once: M ...', 'uncommitted change', '... differs from what the run wrote'): repro-r4 tests 3-6. Still open: checkWriteOnce (rules.mjs:588-597) runs 'git log --no-renames --diff-filter=MDT --name-status' without -m/--diff-merges, so git prints no diff for merge commits. Any change to a committed reviewer artefact made inside a merge commit is invisible. repro-r4 test 10: round evidence is committed with code-security's genuine round-2 verification FAIL/OPEN for High mandatory F-DG0-101. A no-op side branch is merged with --no-commit. In the merge commit, the sidecar becomes PASS/CLOSED_VERIFIED, meta.json outputs are re-pointed, findings.json is mirrored and the gate record is added. git status is clean, and HEAD~1 still holds the FAIL. validateGate (current) returns []. After approveAndCommit, validateGate (historical) and validatePipeline also return [], because checkApprovalImmutable pins whatever the approval commit contains. Test 11 drops a committed round-1 High finding the same way. Test 12 shows the log used prints nothing, while the same command with -m prints 'M ...verifications.json'. The real DG0 history has no merges and no write-once modifications (09 log), so a correct rule would not block DG0. Fix: include merge diffs (-m, or --diff-merges=separate with --full-history), or better, compare each write-once path's current HEAD blob and working-tree bytes with the blob of the commit that first added it (e.g. 'git log --diff-filter=A -m --full-history --format=%H -- <path>'), and require every path ever added to still exist. Add a regression test with an evil merge.

On 540b3c69, round-3 test 9 reproduces: with core.fileMode=false, the working-tree mode disagrees with git (04 log). On candidate 53f5d176, manifestFromWorkingTree takes tracked modes from the index when core.fileMode=false. repro-r4 test 9: after chmod -x of a committed 100755 file and chmod +x of a 100644 file, git status is clean and the working-tree ID equals the committed ID. With core.fileMode=true, a real chmod still changes the ID, so F-DG0-112 has not regressed.

On 540b3c69, round-3 test 10 reproduces: ACCEPTED_OBSERVATION taken from role names typed into findings.json (04 log). On candidate 53f5d176, acceptance is read from the latest per-role sidecar entries with status_after ACCEPTED_OBSERVATION. Each one is bound to its run (checkInvocation with the assignment, freeze and outputs), a specialist and the auditor are both required, and findings.json accepted_by must mirror them. repro-r4 test 8: findings.json-only acceptance is rejected ('no release-auditor sidecar accepts it', 'no specialist reviewer sidecar accepts it'). The candidate's own F-DG0-117 test shows that the properly bound path passes.
